mainTopic: Objections to רבי אליעזר's גט that excludes one man, the meaning of כריתות, and conditions or time limits in a גט.
overview: This amud continues the debate over רבי אליעזר's view that a גט permitting a woman to everyone except one man is valid. First the גמרא shows that one of רבי עקיבא's objections fits only a חוץ case. It then explains that he attacked both חוץ and על מנת because he had heard both versions of the ruling. Next it explains רבא's refutation of the second objection, which follows רבי ינאי's elder and his different source for the rule. רבי יהושע says not to refute 'the lion' after his death, even though he has his own objection: the second marriage must be like the first, with her tied to no one. The גמרא then studies a ברייתא where רבי שמעון בר אלעזר asks where one person forbids and another permits, and it answers challenges from יבמה, נדרים and הפרת הבעל. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה argues from the word כריתות that a גט must fully cut the bond, and רבא rules on a condition not to drink wine, which fails only if it is tied to the wife's own life. Finally רבא asks about a divorce for one day only and begins to answer his own question.

steps.title: With a condition, she is a divorcée even toward that man
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that in a case of על מנת the objection does not work, because the woman is still considered divorced from the forbidden man as far as זנות is concerned.
steps.simpleTranslation: But in that case she is a divorcée with respect to him, as far as licentious relations go!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against reading this objection as being about a גט given על מנת (with a condition).
steps.deeperAnalysis: With על מנת, the husband only stipulated that she may not marry that man. He never forbade זנות with him, so she counts as divorced even toward him. That takes away the קל וחומר the objection depended on.

keyTerms.meaning: a divorced woman
with respect to him (the man who was excluded)
licentious relations outside of marriage
on condition that (a גט with a condition)

phrases.english: Behold, she is a divorcée with respect to him, regarding licentious relations!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי גְּרוּשָׁה אֶצְלוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion about which kind of גט this objection of רבי עקיבא was talking about.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading the objection as being about a גט of על מנת.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: With על מנת she is still a divorcée toward the excluded man for זנות, so the קל וחומר falls apart.

steps.title: So the objection must be about an exception
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that this objection was raised about a גט with an exception (חוץ).
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the objection was about a case of an exception.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the condition reading failed, the גמרא concludes that the objection must refer to a גט of חוץ ("except for so-and-so").
steps.deeperAnalysis: With חוץ, the excluded man is cut out of the divorce completely, so she is not a divorcée toward him at all. That is why the objection's reasoning works only in this case.

keyTerms.meaning: rather
except (a גט that excludes one man)

phrases.english: Rather, it is with regard to "except."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בְּחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion that follows from the rejection in step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: This objection of רבי עקיבא is about a גט of חוץ, not one of על מנת.

steps.title: Why does רבי עקיבא attack both versions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי עקיבא's inconsistency: one objection is about חוץ and another about על מנת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא: if he holds the case is about "except," let him object about "except," and if he holds it is about "on condition," let him object about "on condition"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי עקיבא aims one objection at a גט of חוץ and another at a גט of על מנת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's ruling should be about one specific case. So רבי עקיבא should pick one reading and attack only that. Mixing the two looks inconsistent.

keyTerms.meaning: he holds, he is of the opinion
let him raise an objection

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva, if he holds "except"
phrases.notes: He means: if רבי עקיבא understands רבי אליעזר's ruling as being about a חוץ case.

phrases.english: let him object regarding "except,"
and if he holds "on condition"
let him object regarding "on condition"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, אִי חוּץ סְבִירָא לֵיהּ לוֹתֵיב חוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that one objection is shown to be about חוץ, the גמרא notices that another objection is about על מנת, and it questions that.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's method of objecting to רבי אליעזר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A single ruling has a single case. Attacking two different cases is inconsistent.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא heard two versions of the ruling
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא heard רבי אליעזר's ruling reported both ways, so he refuted each version separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא heard that some say it was about "except" and some say it was about "on condition." For the one who says "except," this is the refutation, and for the one who says "on condition," that is the refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי עקיבא heard two reports of רבי אליעזר's ruling, so he gave a refutation for each.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא was not confused about what he himself held. He was covering both versions of the ruling that were going around. Each objection is aimed at a different version.

keyTerms.meaning: he heard
there is one who says
refutation
the one who says

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא's two objections are aimed at two different reported versions of רבי אליעזר's ruling, one about חוץ and one about על מנת.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva heard
that there is one who says "except"
and there is one who says "on condition";
for the one who says "except", this is the refutation,
and for the one who says "on condition", this is the refutation.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא שְׁמִיעַ לֵיהּ דְּאִיכָּא דְּאָמַר חוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two reported versions of the ruling, each refuted separately.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא held one reading and was inconsistent in attacking both.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was answering both reported versions of רבי אליעזר's ruling.

steps.title: What was the refutation?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the refutation was that רבא found for רבי עקיבא's second objection.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the refutation?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what weakness was found in רבי עקיבא's second objection. This sets up the next move, where a possible answer is tried out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבא accepted one objection but said the second one could be refuted. Now the גמרא wants to know exactly what that refutation is.

keyTerms.meaning: and what

phrases.english: And what is the refutation?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי פִּירְכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about the content of רבא's refutation.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly is the flaw in רבי עקיבא's second objection?

steps.title: Saying the priestly prohibition is different does not work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the refutation might be that the כהונה prohibition is a special case, and then rejects this, because רבי אליעזר himself learns his rule from that very prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we say the prohibition of the priesthood is different, but רבי אליעזר also derives his ruling from the prohibition of the priesthood!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one possible refutation, that the rule about marrying a כהן is a special case. It then knocks it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the כהונה prohibition were a special case, nothing could be learned from it. But רבי אליעזר's own source is the פסוק about a כהן not marrying a woman divorced from her husband. So it cannot be dismissed as irrelevant.

keyTerms.meaning: if we say
the prohibition against marrying a כהן
is different
he derives it

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the גמרא's final answer to "what is the refutation." It is only one proposal that is being rejected.

phrases.english: If we say the prohibition of the priesthood is different,
but Rabbi Eliezer also
derives it from the prohibition of the priesthood!
phrases.notes: His source is ויקרא 21:7, which says a כהן may not marry a woman divorced from her husband.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נֵימָא אִיסּוּר כְּהוּנָּה שָׁאנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to the question in step 5 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the refutation is "the כהונה prohibition is different."
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי אליעזר's own ruling is learned from the כהונה prohibition, so that prohibition cannot be dismissed as a special case.

steps.title: רבא Follows a Different Source for רבי אליעזר's Rule
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns רבי אליעזר's rule the way רבי ינאי taught it in the name of an elder, from a different פסוק. So the כהונה prohibition really can be treated as a special case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא teaches it according to רבי ינאי, who reported it in the name of one elder.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem from step 6. רבא does not hold that רבי אליעזר learns his rule from the כהונה prohibition. He follows a different source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6, the idea that 'כהונה is a special case' was rejected because רבי אליעזר supposedly learns his whole rule from כהונה. Now we hear that רבא follows רבי ינאי's elder, who learns the rule from a different פסוק. If כהונה is not the source of the rule, רבא is free to say that כהונה is different and cannot be compared.

keyTerms.meaning: An early אמורא who reports a teaching he heard from an older scholar
One elder, an unnamed older scholar
He teaches it this way, meaning this is his version of the teaching

phrases.english: Rava — in accordance with Rabbi Yannai
in the name of one elder, he teaches it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא – כְּרַבִּי יַנַּאי מִשּׁוּם זָקֵן אֶחָד קָא מַתְנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rejection in step 6 by changing which source רבא assumes for רבי אליעזר's rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different source: רבא follows a tradition in which רבי אליעזר's rule does not come from כהונה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי אליעזר learns from כהונה, so כהונה could not be called a special case.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא follows רבי ינאי's elder, who uses a different פסוק, so כהונה can be a special case that refutes רבי עקיבא's second objection.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: Don't Refute the Lion After His Death
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings up the next line of the ברייתא: רבי יהושע tells the Sages that one does not refute 'the lion,' רבי אליעזר, after his death.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to them: One does not refute the lion after death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now quotes the next line of the ברייתא it has been discussing. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Sages were raising objections against רבי אליעזר's rule after he had died. רבי יהושע calls רבי אליעזר 'the lion,' a great Torah scholar, and says it is not right to refute him now that he cannot answer back.

keyTerms.meaning: Respond to, refute
Lion, a title for a great Torah scholar
After death

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to them:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְשִׁיבִין אֶת הָאֲרִי לְאַחַר מִיתָה.
phrases.english: One does not refute the lion after death.
phrases.notes: 'The lion' is רבי אליעזר. He can no longer defend his own view.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: אֵין מְשִׁיבִין אֶת הָאֲרִי לְאַחַר מִיתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from רבא's refutation to the next line of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One should not press objections against a great scholar after he has died and can no longer respond.

steps.title: Doesn't רבי יהושע Also Object?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי יהושע agrees with רבי אליעזר. That cannot be right, because רבי יהושע himself raises an objection against him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean רבי יהושע agrees with him? But he himself also raises a refutation!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יהושע's statement. If he is defending רבי אליעזר, it seems he agrees with him, yet we know he also objected to רבי אליעזר's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Don't refute the lion' sounds as if רבי יהושע is taking רבי אליעזר's side. But the גמרא knows that רבי יהושע had his own objection to this rule. So his words seem to contradict his own position.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say, a phrase that opens a challenging question
He holds like him
He actually raises a refutation

phrases.english: Is this to say that Rabbi Yehoshua
holds like him?!
But he too
does raise a refutation!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ כְּווֹתֵיהּ סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges what step 8 seems to imply about רבי יהושע's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that רבי יהושע's statement shows he agrees with רבי אליעזר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהושע has his own objection to רבי אליעזר, so he cannot be agreeing with him.

steps.title: רבי יהושע Holds Back His Own Objection Too
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע meant: 'I also have an objection, but neither mine nor yours should be raised against the lion after his death.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he said to them: I too have a refutation. But whether it is mine or yours, one does not refute the lion after death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רבי יהושע does disagree, but he is saying that nobody, himself included, should press objections now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע's words are about respect, not about agreeing with the הלכה. He admits he has his own objection. Out of honor for רבי אליעזר, he tells everyone to hold back.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he meant, a phrase that introduces an explanation
A refutation or objection
Whether mine or yours

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע disagreed with רבי אליעזר, but he held that one should not press objections against a great teacher after his death.

phrases.english: This is what he said to them:
I too have a refutation;
but whether mine or yours —

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְשִׁיבִין אֶת הָאֲרִי לְאַחַר מִיתָה.
phrases.english: one does not refute the lion after death.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר לְהוּ: לְדִידִי נָמֵי אִית לִי פִּירְכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 9 by explaining what רבי יהושע meant.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the statement is about respect, not about agreeing with the ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהושע's statement showed that he agrees with רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: He has his own objection, but he says no objection, his or theirs, should be pressed after רבי אליעזר's death.

steps.title: What Was רבי יהושע's Objection?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what objection רבי יהושע had against רבי אליעזר's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is רבי יהושע's refutation?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks to hear רבי יהושע's actual objection. This sets up the ברייתא quoted in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 told us that רבי יהושע had an objection but did not tell us what it was. Here the גמרא asks for that missing detail.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is it

phrases.english: And what is Rabbi Yehoshua's refutation?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי פִּירְכָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on step 10's mention that רבי יהושע had an objection.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The content of רבי יהושע's objection to רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: Before the Second Marriage Must Be Like Before the First
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהושע: the פסוק compares a woman before her second marriage to a woman before her first. Just as she was tied to no man the first time, she must be tied to no man the second time.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי יהושע said, the פסוק compares 'before the second marriage' to 'before the first marriage.' Just as before the first marriage she is not tied to any other man, so too before the second marriage she must not be tied to any other man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by quoting a ברייתא that gives רבי יהושע's objection. It is a comparison drawn from the פסוק itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק places her first marriage and her second marriage side by side, so the two must be alike. Before her first marriage she was completely free. So a גט must also leave her completely free, and a גט that still keeps her tied to her first husband in some way does not work. This attacks רבי אליעזר's rule that such a גט is valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Compares one thing to another based on how the פסוק places them together
'Becoming' a wife, a marriage, from the word וְהָיְתָה
The time before
Tied or bound
Another man

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע's objection: a divorce must leave the woman as free as she was before her first marriage, tied to no one.
steps.whyThisMatters: This comparison is the main reason a גט with leftover ties to the husband is a problem. It is the basis for the view against רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Yehoshua said:
[The verse] compares before the second marriage
phrases.notes: The פסוק is דברים 24:1–2. 'הויה' comes from 'וְהָיְתָה', 'and she becomes' a man's wife.

phrases.english: to before the first marriage;
just as before the first marriage —
she is not tied to another man;
so too before the second marriage —
she is not tied to another man.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: מַקִּישׁ קוֹדְמֵי הֲוָיָה שְׁנִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 11 by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהושע compares the second marriage to the first: just as she was tied to no man before the first, she must be tied to no man before the second.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר agrees she may later marry the excluded man
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to a ברייתא it quoted earlier. רבי אליעזר agrees that once the woman's second marriage ends, she may marry the man her first husband excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now let us look at the ברייתא itself. Suppose a man divorces his wife and tells her: 'You may marry anyone except so-and-so.' She then marries a different man, and he dies or divorces her. רבי אליעזר agrees that she may now marry the man she was forbidden to.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to study a ברייתא it mentioned earlier only briefly. This step lays out רבי אליעזר's ruling so the next steps can argue about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that a גט with an exclusion still works. He adds that the exclusion is not permanent. Once a second husband marries her and then releases her, the original limit is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The thing itself.' The גמרא goes back to study in full a source it mentioned earlier in passing.
Agrees, admits. Used when a person concedes a point in a specific case.
Except for so-and-so. This is the exclusion written into the divorce.
Literally 'someone from the market.' It means any ordinary other man.

phrases.english: The matter itself:
Rabbi Eliezer agrees
in the case of one who divorces his wife and said to her:
'You are hereby permitted to any man'
'except for so-and-so,'
and she went and married someone from the general public,
and was widowed or divorced,
that she is permitted to this one to whom she had been forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא – מוֹדֶה רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא referred to this ברייתא in passing earlier in the סוגיא. Now it pauses the elders' ברייתא, quotes this one directly, and studies it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, the exclusion in the גט ends once a second marriage has ended. The woman may then marry the excluded man.

steps.title: Where do we find one man forbidding and another permitting?
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בר אלעזר objects to רבי אליעזר. It makes no sense for the first husband to create a prohibition that a different man, the second husband, can remove.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בר אלעזר answered back against רבי אליעזר's words: Where do we ever find that one person forbids something and a different person permits it?
steps.whatsHappening: Still inside the ברייתא, רבי שמעון בר אלעזר attacks רבי אליעזר's concession. He says there is no other case in the law that works this way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first husband is the one who made her forbidden to 'so-and-so.' Yet under רבי אליעזר, the second husband's marriage and divorce or death removes that prohibition. רבי שמעון בר אלעזר says the law has no example of one man creating a prohibition and another man undoing it.

keyTerms.meaning: Answered back. He raised an objection or refutation.
Forbids, makes something prohibited.
Permits, removes a prohibition.
Where do we find? It asks for a precedent somewhere else in the law.

phrases.aramaic: הֵשִׁיב רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר אֶלְעָזָר תְּשׁוּבָה
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon bar Elazar raised a refutation
against the words of Rabbi Eliezer:
Where do we find
that this one forbids and that one permits?
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the first husband, who made the exclusion. 'That one' is the second husband, whose marriage frees her.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵשִׁיב רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר אֶלְעָזָר תְּשׁוּבָה לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the concession of רבי אליעזר quoted in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's ruling that the second husband's marriage removes the first husband's exclusion.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The law has no case where one person creates a prohibition and a different person removes it.

steps.title: Challenge: the case of a יבמה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רבי שמעון בר אלעזר's objection. It offers יבמה as a case where the husband forbids and the יבם permits.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there really no such case? What about a יבמה? Her husband forbids her, and the יבם permits her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against רבי שמעון בר אלעזר. It claims there is a case where one man forbids and another permits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a man dies without children, his widow cannot marry other men. She is tied to his brother, the יבם. The גמרא reads this as the husband making her forbidden, while the יבם is the one who later sets her free. That would be exactly the 'one forbids, another permits' pattern that רבי שמעון בר אלעזר said does not exist.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And not?!' An astonished challenge: is that really so?
A widow whose husband died without children. She is tied to his brother.
The brother of the husband who died. He must do יבום or חליצה.

steps.confusionAlert: This challenge is not coming from רבי אליעזר's side of the ברייתא. It is the גמרא itself testing whether רבי שמעון בר אלעזר's objection is really true.

phrases.english: And is there not?!
But there is the case of a יבמה,
where the husband forbids and the יבם permits!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא?! וַהֲרֵי יְבָמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim in step 14 that there is no case of one person forbidding and another permitting.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון בר אלעזר's claim that one person never forbids while another permits.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It offers a counterexample. With a יבמה, the husband seems to forbid her and the יבם seems to permit her.

steps.title: With a יבמה, the יבם is the one who forbids
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a יבמה is different. The one who really forbids her is the יבם himself, so the same person both forbids and permits.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is the יבם who makes her forbidden. As far as the husband goes, she would already be free, since his death released her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי שמעון בר אלעזר's objection. It shows that the יבמה case is not really an example of two different people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband's death normally frees his wife to marry anyone. The only reason a יבמה is still tied is that a יבם exists. So the יבם is both the cause of the prohibition and the one who removes it, and רבי שמעון בר אלעזר's objection still stands against רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: There, in that other case.
She is already standing permitted, with nothing tying her down.

steps.whatToRemember: The יבמה case does not break רבי שמעון בר אלעזר's rule. The יבם is the one who forbids her, and he is also the one who permits her. In רבי אליעזר's case, though, the first husband forbids and the second husband permits.

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם, יָבָם הוּא קָא אָסַר לַהּ,
phrases.english: There, it is the יבם who forbids her,
for if it depended on the husband,
phrases.notes: He means: if the husband had no brother at all. Then nothing would hold her back after his death.

phrases.english: she would already be permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם, יָבָם הוּא קָא אָסַר לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the יבמה counterexample from step 15, which keeps step 14's objection in place.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: it shows who really causes the prohibition in a יבמה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: In a יבמה, the husband forbids and the יבם permits.
steps.terutzMaskana: The husband's death frees her. Only the יבם's existence ties her, so the same person forbids and permits.

steps.title: Vows: one person forbids, a sage permits
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון בר אלעזר's rule from נדרים. The person who vows creates the prohibition, but a חכם removes it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about vows? The one who vows makes something forbidden, and a sage makes it permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another case that seems to break the rule that one person cannot forbid while another person permits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בר אלעזר said that the one who forbids must be the one who permits. With נדרים, the person who vows makes the item forbidden, and then a חכם, a different person, releases the vow. This looks like a clear counterexample.

keyTerms.meaning: Vows, where a person makes something forbidden to himself by his words
The person who makes a vow
A Torah scholar who has the power to release vows
Permits or releases

phrases.english: But there are vows,
where the one who vows forbids, and a sage permits!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי נְדָרִים, דְּנוֹדֵר אוֹסֵר וְחָכָם מַתִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the יבמה case was answered in step 16, the גמרא offers a new counterexample to the same rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון בר אלעזר's rule that a different person cannot remove a prohibition someone else created.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With vows, the vower forbids and a separate person, the חכם, permits. So it is possible for one person to forbid and another to permit.

steps.title: A sage releases a vow only through the vower's regret
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says a חכם releases a vow only through the vower's חרטה, regret. So the release really comes from the vower himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי יוחנן said: A sage permits nothing except through regret.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from vows. The חכם is not really the one doing the permitting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חכם can release a vow only when the vower regrets having made it. Since the release depends on the vower's own regret, the person who forbade is really the one undoing it. The חכם only carries it out, so the rule still holds.

keyTerms.meaning: Regret; the vower's feeling that he would not have made the vow
Anything at all

phrases.english: But Rabbi Yochanan has said:
A sage does not permit anything
except through regret.
phrases.notes: He means the regret of the person who made the vow, not the sage's own opinion.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from vows in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining who really permits: the vower's own regret is the true source of the release.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכם, a different person, removes the prohibition the vower created.
steps.terutzMaskana: The release works only through the vower's regret, so the vower himself is really the one undoing his vow.

steps.title: A husband cancels his wife's vow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises הפרת הבעל. The wife makes the vow, and her husband cancels it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about a husband's cancelling of vows? The wife vows, and the husband cancels!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one more case where one person seems to forbid and a different person permits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here no regret is needed from the wife. The husband can cancel her vow on his own. So the answer about the חכם does not seem to work here.

keyTerms.meaning: A husband's power to cancel his wife's vows
Cancels a vow

phrases.english: But there is the husband's cancelling of vows,
where the wife vows and the husband cancels!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי הֲפָרַת הַבַּעַל, דְּאִשָּׁה נוֹדֶרֶת וּבַעַל מֵיפֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the vow case was answered with regret, the גמרא brings a case where no regret is involved.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון בר אלעזר's rule that the one who forbids must be the one who permits.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wife creates the prohibition and the husband removes it without her regret. So a different person really does permit.

steps.title: A wife vows with her husband's consent in mind
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with רב פנחס in the name of רבא: every woman who vows does so on her husband's consent. So her vow was limited from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is like what רב פנחס said in the name of רבא: Any woman who vows, vows depending on her husband's consent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from הפרת הבעל by explaining how a wife's vow works from the very beginning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wife makes her vow with the understanding that it depends on her husband agreeing. When he cancels it, he is not undoing her prohibition from outside. Her own vow was built to depend on him, so the rule still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Based on the understanding or consent of
In the name of
There, in that case

steps.whatToRemember: In every case raised against רבי שמעון בר אלעזר (יבמה, a חכם, a husband), the גמרא shows that the 'permitting' really comes from the same source that forbade.

phrases.english: There, it is like Rav Pinchas in the name of Rava,
as Rav Pinchas said in the name of Rava:
Any woman who vows,
vows depending on her husband's consent.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם כִּדְרַב פִּנְחָס מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from הפרת הבעל in step 19 and closes this line of challenges.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the original prohibition: the vow was dependent on the husband from the start.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The husband, a different person, removes a prohibition his wife created.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wife's vow was made depending on her husband's consent, so his cancelling is part of the vow itself.

steps.title: A גט must fully cut the bond
steps.stepSummary: Returning to the ברייתא of the elders against רבי אליעזר, רבי אלעזר בן עזריה argues that כריתות means a full cutting between husband and wife. A גט that excludes one man does not fully cut the bond.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה responded and said: 'כריתות' means something that cuts between him and her. So you have learned that this is not כריתות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the earlier ברייתא and quotes another elder's argument against רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה calls a גט a ספר כריתות, a document of cutting. A גט that says 'you may marry anyone except so-and-so' still leaves the husband with a hold on her, so the cut is not complete. Because of this, it does not count as a valid גט.

keyTerms.meaning: Severance; a complete cutting of the marriage bond
Responded
That which cuts

phrases.aramaic: נַעֲנָה רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה וְאָמַר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya responded and said:
"Severance":
phrases.notes: From the words ספר כריתות, the תורה's name for a גט (דברים 24:1).

phrases.english: means something that cuts between him and her;
so you have learned that this is not severance.
phrases.notes: 'This' means a גט that leaves one man forbidden to her.

steps.triggerLanguage: נַעֲנָה רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה וְאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After closing the side discussion about רבי שמעון בר אלעזר, the גמרא returns to the ברייתא of the elders.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט must completely cut the bond. A גט that excludes one man is not כריתות and does not work.

steps.title: How do the רבנן use the word כריתות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the other רבנן learn from the word כריתות, since they did not use it to argue against רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, what do they do with this word 'כריתות'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move by asking what the other Sages learn from the word כריתות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every word in the תורה is expected to teach something. If the רבנן did not learn רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's point from כריתות, the גמרא wants to know what lesson they do take from it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, here the other elders who did not argue this way
What do they do with it? What do they learn from it?

phrases.english: And the Rabbis, this word "severance",
what do they do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן, הַאי כְּרִיתוּת מַאי עָבְדִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's use of כריתות by asking how the other Sages use the same word.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson the רבנן learn from the word כריתות.

steps.title: A condition that ties her forever is not כריתות
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן use כריתות for a ברייתא about conditions in a גט. A condition that holds her forever is not כריתות, but a condition for thirty days is.
steps.simpleTranslation: They need it for what was taught in a ברייתא: 'This is your גט on condition that you do not drink wine,' or 'on condition that you do not go to your father's house.' If he means forever, this is not כריתות. If he means thirty days, this is כריתות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן use the word כריתות to teach which conditions are allowed in a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A condition that ties the wife to her husband's demand for the rest of her life keeps a lasting bond, so it is not a real cutting. A condition limited to thirty days ends, and after that she is fully free. The רבנן learn this from כריתות instead of using it against רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: On condition that
Your bill of divorce
Forever
They need it for (a different teaching)

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree that a condition binding her forever makes the גט fail. The רבנן learn this from the word כריתות. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה also uses כריתות to rule out a גט that excludes one man, and step 24 explains where he gets the conditions rule.
steps.confusionAlert: The condition in the גט is not the problem. The problem is only a condition with no end, which keeps her tied to her husband for good.

phrases.english: They need it for what was taught in a baraita:
"This is your bill of divorce
on condition that you do not drink wine;

phrases.aramaic: עַל מְנָת שֶׁלֹּא תֵּלְכִי לְבֵית אָבִיךְ״;
phrases.english: on condition that you do not go to your father's house";
"forever": this is not severance.
"thirty days": this is severance.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיבְּעֵי לְהוּ לְכִדְתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22 about how the רבנן use the word כריתות.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן learn from כריתות that a condition that binds her forever makes the גט invalid, while a time-limited condition such as thirty days is fine.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's source for the law of conditions
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה used כריתות to teach a full cutting. He learns the law of conditions from the fact that the תורה says כריתות and not the shorter כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one (רבי אלעזר בן עזריה)? He learns it from the difference between כרת and כריתות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבי אלעזר בן עזריה learns the rule about conditions in a גט, since he already used the word כריתות for something else. It answers that he learns it from the longer form of the word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 23 the רבנן learned the conditions rule from כריתות. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה already used כריתות to rule out a גט that excludes one man. The longer form כריתות, used instead of the basic כרת, gives him room for a second lesson, so he learns the conditions rule from that too.

keyTerms.meaning: The other one; here, the other opinion
The basic, shorter form of the word for 'cutting'
The longer form of the word, used in the פסוק 'ספר כריתות'
It comes out; he learns it from

phrases.english: And the other one?
phrases.notes: This means רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

phrases.english: He learns it from 'karet' versus 'keritut.'
phrases.notes: The תורה could have used the short form כרת but wrote the longer כריתות, which leaves room for an extra lesson.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידָּךְ – מִ״כָּרֵת–כְּרִיתוּת״ נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors Step 22–23: now asks the same 'where from' question about רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He learns the conditions rule from the use of the longer word כריתות instead of כרת.

steps.title: The רבנן do not learn from the כרת/כריתות difference
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן do not read any lesson into the difference between כרת and כריתות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other ones (the רבנן)? They do not learn anything from כרת versus כריתות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the רבנן do with the longer form of the word. It answers that they do not learn anything from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains why the רבנן have only one lesson from the word כריתות, the conditions rule. They do not treat the longer form as a second hint. So they have no source for רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's 'full cutting' lesson.

keyTerms.meaning: They do not expound; they learn no lesson from it

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן learn the conditions rule from the word כריתות itself. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה uses כריתות for his 'full cutting' point against רבי אליעזר, and learns the conditions rule from the longer form כרת/כריתות, which the רבנן do not expound.

phrases.english: And the other ones?
phrases.notes: Now it means the רבנן. What do they do with the longer form of the word?

phrases.english: They do not expound 'karet' versus 'keritut.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ – ״כָּרֵת–כְּרִיתוּת״ לָא דָּרְשִׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the pair of questions by explaining the רבנן's side.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן do not learn anything from the difference between כרת and כריתות.

steps.title: רבא: a גט on condition she not drink wine
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules on a גט given on condition that the wife not drink wine. If the condition lasts 'all the days of my life,' it is not כריתות. If it lasts 'all the days of so-and-so's life,' it is כריתות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: 'Here is your גט on condition that you do not drink wine.' If he says 'all the days of my life,' that is not a cutting. If he says 'all the days of so-and-so's life,' that is a cutting.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new ruling that applies the idea of כריתות to a real condition. It is a condition not to drink wine for a set time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether such a condition still leaves her tied to the husband. In this first version, a condition tied to the husband's own life is not a real cutting. A condition tied to another person's life does count as a cutting. The גמרא will soon question this split.

keyTerms.meaning: On condition that
Your bill of divorce
All the days of my life
So-and-so; some other person

phrases.english: Rava said:
'Here is your bill of divorce,'
on condition that you do not drink wine';
if he says 'all the days of my life,' that is not a cutting.
If he says 'all the days of so-and-so's life,'
that is a cutting.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: ״הֲרֵי זֶה גִּיטִּיךְ, עַל מְנָת שֶׁלֹּא תִּשְׁתִּי יַיִן״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the כריתות rule about conditions from Step 23 to a specific case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A condition not to drink wine for the husband's life is not כריתות. For another person's life it is כריתות (first version).

steps.title: Why is the husband's life different from another person's life?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא: if 'so-and-so's life' works because he may die and free her, the husband may also die and free her.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about so-and-so's life? Is it because he might die and she will have fulfilled her condition? The husband might also die, and she will have fulfilled her condition!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the first version of רבא's ruling. It argues that the husband's life and another person's life should be the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only reason 'so-and-so's life' could count as a cutting is that he might die in her lifetime. Then she would be free of the condition. But the husband might die in her lifetime too, so the two cases should have the same law.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different?
Perhaps
She fulfills his condition

phrases.english: What is different about so-and-so's life?
Is it because perhaps he will die
and she will have fulfilled his condition?
With his own life, too,
perhaps he will die,
and she will have fulfilled his condition!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא חַיֵּי פְלוֹנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the distinction drawn in Step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's split between 'my life' (not כריתות) and 'so-and-so's life' (כריתות).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both people could die while she is alive and end the condition, so there is no reason to treat them differently.

steps.title: Corrected version: only 'all the days of your life' fails
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes רבא's wording. 'All the days of your life' is not כריתות, but 'all the days of my life' or 'so-and-so's life' is כריתות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: 'all the days of your life' is not a cutting. 'All the days of my life' or 'so-and-so's life' is a cutting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by changing what רבא actually said. The line between the cases now depends on whose life the condition lasts for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A condition for her whole life never ends while she is alive, so she is never fully cut free. The husband's life and another person's life can both end while she is still alive, so both count as a cutting. This puts the husband's case together with 'so-and-so' and answers the question in Step 27.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say; the wording should be changed to
All the days of your (her) life

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. In the final version, 'all the days of my life' (the husband's life) does count as כריתות. Only 'your life' (the wife's) does not.
steps.whatToRemember: A condition that can never end while she is alive is not כריתות. A condition that might end while she is alive (tied to the husband or another person) is כריתות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This makes the rule from Step 23 concrete. The test is whether the condition could end while she is still alive.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
'all the days of your life'
that is not a cutting;
'all the days of my life' or 'so-and-so's life'
that is a cutting.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא: ״כׇּל יְמֵי חַיֵּיכִי״ – אֵין זֶה כְּרִיתוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 27 by changing the wording of רבא's statement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the wording of the statement (אלא אימא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא was thought to say that the husband's life is not כריתות and another person's life is.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a condition for the wife's own life is not כריתות. The husband's life or another person's life is כריתות.

steps.title: רבא asks about a divorce that lasts only one day
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב נחמן what the law is if a husband gives a גט and says, 'Today you are not my wife, and tomorrow you are my wife.' The question can be asked according to both רבי אליעזר and the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked רב נחמן: If a husband says, 'Today you are not my wife, and tomorrow you are my wife,' what is the law? You can ask this according to רבי אליעזר, and you can ask it according to the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a new question about a גט that cuts the marriage off for only a limited time. The גמרא says the question works on both sides of the מחלוקת in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי אליעזר and the רבנן argue about a גט that says 'you are permitted to any man except so-and-so.' That גט limits the divorce by person. רבא's case limits it by time instead, so it is unclear how each side would rule.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (a real question, not an attack)
What is the law?
Let the question be asked (according to this opinion)
The תנא in the משנה who says the 'except so-and-so' גט is valid
The Sages, who say that גט is not valid

phrases.english: Rava asked Rav Nachman:
"Today you are not my wife,
and tomorrow you are my wife" — what is the law?
Ask it according to Rabbi Eliezer,
ask it according to the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רָבָא מֵרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: a time-limited divorce rather than a גט with a condition.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a גט work if it frees her only for today and she returns to being his wife tomorrow?

steps.title: The doubt according to רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: Maybe רבי אליעזר approves the 'except so-and-so' גט only because the permission he gives to the other men lasts forever. A one-day divorce has no such permanence, so maybe it fails. Or maybe there is no difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: Ask it according to רבי אליעזר: Maybe רבי אליעזר says the גט works there only because whoever he permits her to, he permits her forever. But here, it does not work. Or maybe there is no difference.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the question is real for רבי אליעזר. It gives two possible ways he might rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the 'except so-and-so' גט permits her to everyone else permanently. In רבא's case she is free only for one day, and then she becomes his wife again. So maybe רבי אליעזר would not accept a gap in time, even though he accepts a gap in people. Or maybe he sees both cases the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: He only said his ruling up to this point (in that case)
Permits
Forever
Or perhaps it is no different

phrases.english: Ask it according to Rabbi Eliezer:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הָתָם,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer only said his ruling there
phrases.notes: 'There' means the משנה's case, 'you are permitted to any man except so-and-so.'

phrases.english: because whoever he does permit her to,
he permits her forever;
but here — no.
Or perhaps it is no different.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּיבְּעֵי לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר – עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first half of the question from step 29.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי אליעזר need the permission to be permanent, or is a time-limited freedom also fine?

steps.title: The doubt according to the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: Maybe the רבנן reject the 'except so-and-so' גט only because the husband did not cut her off from himself completely. In רבא's case he fully cuts her off for a time, so maybe that counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Ask it according to the רבנן: Maybe the רבנן say the גט fails there only because he did not cut her off from himself completely. But here, once he cut her off, she is cut off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the question is real for the רבנן too. Here it suggests a reason the גט might work even according to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן disqualify the משנה's גט because one man stays forbidden to her, so the break is not complete. In רבא's case, for that one day the break is total: she is free to marry anyone. Maybe a complete break, even a short one, is enough for the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: He cut her off (separated her)
Completely
Since, once

steps.confusionAlert: Notice the two sides point in opposite directions. For רבי אליעזר the worry is that the גט might fail. For the רבנן the new idea is that it might work.

phrases.english: Ask it according to the Rabbis:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי רַבָּנַן הָתָם,
phrases.english: the Rabbis only said their ruling there
because he did not cut her off from himself completely;
but here, once he cut her off, she is cut off.
phrases.notes: The 'or perhaps it is no different' is left unsaid here, but the גמרא means it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּיבְּעֵי לְרַבָּנַן – עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי רַבָּנַן הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second half of the question from step 29.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do the רבנן only need a complete break, even if it is temporary?

steps.title: רבא turns around to answer his own question
steps.stepSummary: After asking the question, רבא himself goes back and resolves it. The answer comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: After he asked it, he went back and resolved it:
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. It tells us that רבא is about to answer his own question, and the answer follows right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No ruling is given yet. The line only shows that the same person who asked will now give the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: After he asked it
He went back and resolved it

phrases.english: After he asked it,
he went back and resolved it:
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבא himself, not רב נחמן.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּתַר דְּבַעְיָא, הֲדַר פַּשְׁטַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the two-sided question to רבא's own answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not yet stated; this line only introduces רבא's resolution.
